clients.name: Claude Code
clients.mechanism: Remote MCP over HTTP (recommended), SSE (deprecated; v2.1.265+ tries HTTP then falls back), stdio, WebSocket, in-process SDK. Also plugins, skills, CLAUDE.md context files.
clients.auth: OAuth 2.0 via /mcp or `claude mcp login`; dynamic client registration; pre-registered client id/secret and callback port; oauth.authServerMetadataUrl and oauth.scopes overrides; static headers (Authorization: Bearer). Per-user.
clients.org_distribution: managed-mcp.json for exclusive control, managedMcpServers to provide servers to every user, allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers filtering by serverName or serverUrl, managed plugin marketplaces.
clients.limits: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS default 25,000 tokens (warning above 10,000). Results over 50,000 chars are saved to a file unless the tool sets _meta anthropic/maxResultSizeChars (hard ceiling 500,000 chars). Tool search defers tool definitions; tool _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad exempts a tool; server instructions capped at 4,096 characters.
clients.mcp_features: Tools, prompts, resources, elicitation, list_changed refresh; deferred loading via tool search.
clients.caveats: A JSON entry with url but no type is read as stdio and rejected. Tool search can hide tools, so write precise names and descriptions.

clients.name: Claude Code managed MCP
clients.mechanism: Admin-delivered config file plus allow/deny policy.
clients.auth: Same as Claude Code; allow/deny matched on serverName or serverUrl.
clients.org_distribution: managed-mcp.json, managedMcpServers, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers. Page text was only partly read, so details beyond these names are not captured.
clients.limits: Not stated in the part read.
clients.caveats: Only the names of the controls were confirmed from the MCP page; the managed-mcp page itself was not read in full.

clients.name: Claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Cowork (custom connectors)
clients.mechanism: Remote MCP server added as a custom connector under Customize > Connectors. Local servers in claude_desktop_config.json are a separate mechanism, not available in Cowork or claude.ai.
clients.auth: Sign in now / when needed / no sign in. OAuth client options: Claude's published identity (recommended), automatic registration, or the user's own client. Fixed headers (API key, bearer) stored encrypted. Each member connects individually after an admin adds it; a shared credential gives everyone that credential's access.
clients.org_distribution: Team: Owners and Primary Owners add org connectors. Enterprise: Owners, Primary Owners and custom roles with Manage access to Libraries. Free plan limited to one custom connector.
clients.mcp_features: Tools; interactive connectors can render inline cards or fullscreen apps; Team and Enterprise owners can disable specific tool calls that render them. Resources and prompts not described.
clients.caveats: Connections come from Anthropic's cloud, so private or VPN servers need Anthropic IP ranges allowlisted. Connectors are not verified by Anthropic. Advanced research cannot invoke tools from local servers.

clients.name: Claude API MCP connector
clients.mechanism: `mcp_servers` parameter in the Messages API; server must be publicly exposed over HTTP (Streamable HTTP or SSE). Local stdio servers cannot be connected directly.
clients.auth: Caller supplies an OAuth access token in `authorization_token`; the caller runs the OAuth flow.
clients.org_distribution: Not applicable; the application owner configures it per request.
clients.limits: Beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20. Not ZDR-eligible (from saved page text).
clients.mcp_features: Tools only (per the page text read).
clients.caveats: Public URL required; token handling is the caller's job.

clients.name: Claude Agent Skills
clients.mechanism: A directory with SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter plus Markdown). Description stays in context; body and supporting files load on demand (progressive disclosure). Open Agent Skills standard.
clients.auth: Not applicable (files, not a network service). A skill can instruct Claude to call the brain's MCP tools.
clients.org_distribution: Enterprise skills directory inside managed settings; skills inside plugins from marketplaces; claude.ai skills sync to ~/.claude/skills/synced/. Managed controls include strictPluginOnlyCustomization and skillOverrides.
clients.limits: description plus when_to_use truncated at 1,536 chars in the listing; keep SKILL.md under 500 lines; compatibility up to 500 chars; after compaction each skill re-attaches first 5,000 tokens, 25,000 combined.
clients.mcp_features: Not an MCP feature; complements an MCP server by teaching when and how to use it.
clients.caveats: claude.ai and the Skills API accept only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools; other frontmatter fields hard-error on upload.

clients.name: OpenAI Codex (CLI, IDE, app)
clients.mechanism: config.toml (~/.codex/config.toml or .codex/config.toml in trusted projects) shared by the ChatGPT desktop app, CLI and IDE extension. STDIO and Streamable HTTP servers.
clients.auth: OAuth by default (`codex mcp login`); supports Client ID Metadata Documents and Dynamic Client Registration; pre-registered client via --oauth-client-id; bearer_token_env_var, http_headers, http_headers_helper; auth=chatgpt for trusted first-party servers only.
clients.org_distribution: Enterprise `mcp_servers` requirement in Agent Security applies to local executors; admins control plugins and tools per workspace; MCP hooks on the cloud coordinator.
clients.limits: startup_timeout_sec default 10, tool_timeout_sec default 60, output_token_limit per tool, enabled_tools/disabled_tools, default_tools_approval_mode (auto, prompt, writes, approve).
clients.mcp_features: Tools (approval modes); other primitives not stated in the summary read.
clients.caveats: ChatGPT web does not read local Codex config. Local servers and transports may not be reachable from cloud containers, which follow Work Cloud policies; check connectivity and auth separately.

clients.name: ChatGPT apps and MCP (deep research, company knowledge)
clients.mechanism: Remote MCP server added as a custom MCP server and created as a plugin; or Responses API tool of type `mcp`. Compatibility needs read-only `search` (query -> results with id, title, url) and `fetch` (id -> id, title, text, url, optional metadata) tools, returned as structuredContent and repeated as JSON text in content.
clients.auth: OAuth. Client ID Metadata Documents recommended where supported (public client or private_key_jwt); dynamic client registration still supported. Workspace users go through OAuth to your service.
clients.org_distribution: Admin enables developer mode and apps at workspace level (admin detail comes from search snippets and a third-party guide; the OpenAI help pages returned 403).
clients.limits: Declare an output schema per tool. Citations are created only when url is a non-empty string.
clients.mcp_features: Tools; apps UI via Apps SDK (not covered on the page read).
clients.caveats: The API docs page example used SSE and did not cover streamable HTTP. Admin and company-knowledge details are snippet-level only.

clients.name: ChatGPT company knowledge and developer mode (admin side)
clients.mechanism: Admin-gated custom MCP connectors; company knowledge uses connected sources.
clients.auth: Per search snippets: apps and connectors off by default on Enterprise and Edu, owner or admin enables at org level; developer mode toggle in workspace permissions.
clients.caveats: Not fetched: help.openai.com returned 403, so only search snippets (and a third-party guide) back this entry.

clients.name: Cursor
clients.mechanism: mcp.json: project .cursor/mcp.json and global ~/.cursor/mcp.json. stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP; variable interpolation in url and headers.
clients.auth: OAuth authorization code with PKCE; discovers the auth server through RFC 9728 protected resource metadata; dynamic client registration as a public client; static OAuth via auth.CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/scopes with fixed redirect URLs; static headers.
clients.org_distribution: Not covered on the page read (no org distribution content found there).
clients.limits: Asks approval before running tools by default; no tool-count limit stated in the part read.
clients.mcp_features: Tools, prompts, resources, roots, elicitation, and the Apps extension (UI), with graceful fallback when UI cannot render.
clients.caveats: Cursor team distribution and allowlist were in earlier research but not confirmed from a fetched page, so they are not claimed here.

clients.name: GitHub Copilot
clients.mechanism: VS Code 1.99+ (.vscode/mcp.json or settings), Visual Studio 17.14+, JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse. Remote URL servers and local command servers.
clients.auth: OAuth for remote servers in Visual Studio (scopes approved in browser); PAT headers or env variables in other IDEs.
clients.org_distribution: Org and enterprise policy 'MCP servers in Copilot', disabled by default, applies to Copilot Business and Enterprise only. GitHub MCP Registry (public preview) is the only source for in-IDE registry installs; other servers are configured manually.
clients.mcp_features: Tools in every IDE; prompts (slash commands) and resources documented for VS Code only.
clients.caveats: Policy does not govern Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max plans. Registry is public-only.

clients.name: Gemini CLI
clients.mechanism: settings.json mcpServers: stdio, SSE (`url`) and Streamable HTTP (`httpUrl`).
clients.auth: OAuth 2.0 for remote servers with auto-discovery after a 401, tokens in ~/.gemini/mcp-oauth-tokens.json, RFC 9207 iss validation, Google credential types; static headers (-H). Needs a local browser.
clients.org_distribution: Only per-user mcp.allowed and mcp.excluded lists in settings.json; no admin allowlist covered.
clients.limits: No tool-count or output limits stated; default request timeout 600,000 ms; tool names over 63 chars are truncated.
clients.caveats: trust:true bypasses all confirmations. Avoid underscores in server names (policy parser splits on them). Headless or SSH sessions cannot complete OAuth.

clients.name: Gemini Enterprise
clients.mechanism: Page for connecting MCP servers returned 404.
clients.caveats: GAP: no primary page was read; do not rely on this entry.

clients.name: Windsurf / Devin Desktop (Cascade)
clients.mechanism: ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json (mcpServers); stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE; env and file interpolation.
clients.auth: OAuth supported for each transport type; headers.
clients.org_distribution: Team and Enterprise admins toggle MCP and allowlist servers (server ID, exact config, or full-string regex). Allowlisting one server blocks all others. Enterprise can set custom registry URLs (no effect on Cascade).
clients.limits: Cascade accesses at most 100 tools at any time; individual tools disabled via disabledTools.
clients.caveats: Page covers the legacy Cascade agent; Devin Local uses other config. Enterprise users must turn MCP on manually. Allowlist matching is case-sensitive.

clients.name: Goose
clients.mechanism: Extensions are MCP servers: stdio command extensions and `streamable_http` remote extensions; config in ~/.config/goose/config.yaml.
clients.auth: OAuth with Client ID Metadata Documents or Dynamic Client Registration, or manual client_id/client_secret_key and scopes; callback on 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port (GOOSE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT to fix it). Custom headers not documented.
clients.org_distribution: No managed rollout documented; central extensions directory and goose:// deeplinks.
clients.mcp_features: Tools; supports MCP Apps per the MCP Apps client list.
clients.caveats: Operates autonomously by default; configure permission modes. Extensions are scanned for known malware before activation.

clients.name: Other MCP Apps hosts (VS Code Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Postman, MCPJam, Archestra)
clients.mechanism: MCP Apps extension: tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri pointing at a ui:// HTML resource rendered in a sandboxed iframe.
clients.caveats: Host support varies; tools must still work as plain text.

brain_products.name: Glean
brain_products.integrates_via: Remote MCP server per tenant (endpoint copied from the MCP Configurator, /mcp/{server}); Streamable HTTP; hosts include Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Goose, VS Code, Windsurf. OAuth via Glean authorization server with DCR, static clients, IdP OAuth, or API token fallback.

brain_products.name: Guru, Moveworks, Claude enterprise search and Google Drive connectors

mcp_spec.fact: Optional; HTTP transports follow it, stdio should not. Built on OAuth 2.1 draft, RFC 8414, RFC 7591 (DCR), RFC 9728 (protected resource metadata) and OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents.
Streamable HTTP and stdio are the standard transports; legacy HTTP+SSE is deprecated.
Experimental task utility for long-running requests.

Two modes: form (flat primitive schema, never for secrets) and url (out-of-band, for credentials and third-party OAuth). Three actions: accept, decline, cancel. In the 2026-07-28 spec it is delivered through multi round-trip requests (InputRequiredResult).

No initialize handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id; each request carries version and capabilities in _meta; Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers required on Streamable HTTP; optional server/discover; sampling, elicitation and roots move to multi round-trip requests; legacy SSE deprecated with a one-year offramp.
Servers should return RFC 9207 iss and clients must validate it; clients set application_type in DCR; credentials bound to issuer; DCR formally deprecated in favor of CIMD.

Tasks move to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension with poll-based tasks/get and tasks/update; subscriptions/listen replaces the GET stream; extensions framework names Tasks, MCP Apps and Enterprise Managed Authorization.
Spec changelog page was fetched; the blog post above is the source for the summary facts.

Priorities: HTTP-native transport, tasks and agentic messaging, enterprise auth and agent identity (EMA stable), improved primitives and progressive discovery, SDK experience. Server Card working group on .well-known metadata.
Public servers only; does not support private servers (private network hosts or private package registries). In preview, with possible breaking changes or data resets.

Extension: tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri to a ui:// resource rendered in a sandboxed iframe; supported by Claude, Claude Desktop, VS Code Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Goose, Postman and others.
Covered in the fetched 2025-11-25 authorization page (resource indicators and PKCE S256); exact quotes not extracted in this pass.

design_implications: Expose one remote Streamable HTTP MCP server, stateless-friendly for the 2026-07-28 spec; keep an SSE-free design.

Implement RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, accept CIMD client ids with DCR as fallback, validate audience (RFC 8707), require PKCE, return RFC 9207 iss, and support a static pre-registered client for Slack-style and Cursor static OAuth hosts.
Ship `search` and `fetch` tools returning {id,title,text,url} so ChatGPT deep research and company knowledge work; add richer tools for others.
Keep the tool count small (Windsurf caps at 100; Claude Code defers tools via tool search) with precise names and descriptions; keep server instructions under 4,096 characters.
Set anthropic/maxResultSizeChars on large tools, keep default results under 25,000 tokens, paginate, and set alwaysLoad only on the one entry tool.

Point, do not copy: run each tool call as the signed-in user and enforce source ACLs at query time, as Notion, Atlassian, Slack and Sourcegraph do. Index-and-copy products (Glean, Onyx, Mem0) carry their own permission-sync burden.
Per-user OAuth is the norm; shared credentials give everyone the same access (Claude connectors, Dust bearer tokens), so avoid them for permissioned data.

Org rollout: managed-mcp.json and managedMcpServers (Claude Code), Owners add org connectors (Claude.ai Team and Enterprise), Copilot 'MCP servers in Copilot' policy, Windsurf allowlist, Codex enterprise mcp_servers requirement, ChatGPT admin-enabled apps.
Ship a Claude plugin with a skill and CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md snippets that tell agents when to query the brain.
Claude.ai connectors call from Anthropic's cloud, so private deployments must allowlist Anthropic IP ranges and expose a public HTTPS URL.
Do not rely on the public MCP Registry for a private brain; use a private registry or direct config distribution.
Use URL-mode elicitation (not form mode) when the brain needs a user to connect a source app, and plan for the Tasks extension for slow multi-source queries.
Gaps to close before relying on this: Gemini Enterprise, ChatGPT admin pages (403), Guru, Moveworks, Zep, Claude Drive connectors, Cursor team distribution.
